original_question: If a Banach space X is strongly weakly K-analytic, or strongly weakly countably determined, must the Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p(μ, X) inherit the same corresponding property?
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core mathematical content essentially correctly: it identifies the two exact properties at issue (strongly weakly K-analytic and strongly weakly countably determined) and asks whether the corresponding Lebesgue-Bochner space L^p(μ, X) inherits them from X. That is exactly the substance of Problem 5.3.
missing_details: Section 5 fixes a probability space (Ω, Σ, μ); the measure is not left completely arbitrary in the paper’s setup.
The paper’s global convention is that all Banach spaces are real.
To make the question fully stand-alone, L^p(μ, X) should be identified as the Banach space of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f: Ω → X such that ∫Ω ||f||^p dμ < ∞.
The paper asks the two cases separately, in the form “strongly WKA (respectively, strongly WCD)”.

The nearby context makes clear that the intent is an inheritance problem for Lebesgue-Bochner spaces, parallel to the already known transfer of WKA and WCD from X to L^p(μ, X), and adjacent to the SWCG inheritance problem.

The paper does not restate the formal definitions of “strongly WKA” and “strongly WCD”; for a completely autonomous formulation one would need either those standard definitions or an explicit reference to the notions discussed in [76, 77, 91], which are the references cited in the paper’s nearby context.
refined_question: Let (Ω, Σ, μ) be a probability space, let X be a real Banach space, and let 1 ≤ p < ∞. Denote by L^p(μ, X) the Banach space of equivalence classes of strongly measurable functions f: Ω → X such that ∫Ω ||f||^p dμ < ∞. If X is strongly weakly K-analytic (respectively, strongly weakly countably determined), must L^p(μ, X) also be strongly weakly K-analytic (respectively, strongly weakly countably determined)?
justification: The exact target is Problem 5.3. Section 5 first fixes the ambient data for Lebesgue-Bochner spaces: a probability space (Ω, Σ, μ), a Banach space X, and 1 ≤ p < ∞, and defines L^p(μ, X). In the immediately preceding context in Section 5.1, the paper frames a generic inheritance question of the form “if X has property (P), does L^p(μ, X) have (P) as well?”, recalls that WKA and WCD are already known to pass from X to L^p(μ, X), and then places Problem 5.3 right after the adjacent SWCG problem. So your draft is very close to the paper’s intent, but it omits the paper’s local setup for μ and p, the global convention that Banach spaces are real, and the explicit separate formulation of the two properties.
